text:
Marathon Petroleum rose 2.8% today, continuing a strong two-week rally that has lifted the stock 11%. The immediate catalyst appears to be oil market volatility—U.S. crude fell below $100 a barrel today after a multiday run higher, but refineries are running at 97.8% capacity with tight fuel inventories (gasoline and diesel storage both well below historical norms), which supports margins for companies turning crude into fuel. The geopolitical backdrop of the Iran war and Houthi threats to Red Sea shipping have kept crude prices elevated and volatile even as they dip intraday.

The broader context here is that refiner profitability depends on the gap between crude costs and fuel prices—and right now that spread is being supported by constrained supply chains and strong refining demand despite lower crude prices. The combination of high capacity utilization, tight product inventories, and ongoing energy disruptions from Middle East tensions has kept conditions favorable for refiners over the past two weeks.
